story.value: Ytterbium is named after Ytterby, a village in Sweden where the mineral ytterbite was originally found.
Ytterbium was discovered in 1878 by the Swiss chemist Jean-Charles Galissard de Marignac.
In 1907, Urbain separated ytterbium into two elements.

uses.value: Ytterbium can be alloyed with stainless steel to improve some of its mechanical properties.
Ytterbium is used as a doping agent in fiber optic cable, where it can be used as an amplifier.
An isotope of ytterbium is reported to have been used as a radiation source for a portable X-ray machine where electricity is unavailable.
